newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS-Portugal says can stick to EMU budget limits.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Portugal says can stick to EMU budget limits.

text.p: Portuguese Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said on Wednesday that the country planned a budget deficit of just two percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1999, well below single European currency limits.
He told journalists that the budget forecast was contained in a financial plan for the years 1997-99 that the government would send to the European Union in March.
A three percent deficit ceiling in 1997 is one of the key entry qualifications for European Union member countries seeking to take part in economic and monetary union (EMU) at its launch in 1999.
Portugal has budgeted for a deficit of 2.9 percent this year but the minister said the figure could be lower, particularly if the economy grew faster than initially expected.
"It is very early to make forecasts (but) I think that it is possible (to have a deficit below target) just as happened last year," he told journalists.
Portugal, which has made qualifying for EMU its top policy priority, had a budget deficit of four percent of GDP in 1996, below the 4.3 percent initially forecast.

Some northern European political and business leaders have expressed reservations about southern European countries such as Portugal joining the single currency at the start, saying that they do not have a history of financial discipline.
But Sousa Franco said the government was confident not only of reducing the deficit in 1997 but of maintaining the downward trend in the following two years.
"We think it is possible to assure a reduction of the deficit and the level of public debt," he said.
